description: Step inside the legendary De Lane Lea Studios at 75 Dean Street, now home to the Museum of Soho, and discover the stories, sounds and creativity that have shaped this remarkable neighbourhood. As part of Open House, enjoy a programme of talks, screenings and conversations celebrating Soho's unique spirit of innovation, diversity and cultural influence.

events.name: Soho - Saints and Sinners
events.notes: Chris Barlow gives us a whistle stop tour of Soho to whet our appetites for our adventures ahead in Soho!

events.name: Hedonism As Activism
events.notes: Fashion & Luxury PR Amar challenges us to consider the role of Fashion & Luxury in shaping social attitudes. Introducing the Gaydian Angels

events.name: The Joy of Discovering Musical Theatre
events.notes: Westminster Blue Badge Guide Roberto shares his journey from Uruguay to London and how Musical Theatre became the touchstone of his new life

events.name: Our Soho - Award winning documentary
events.notes: Screening of Toulouse award winning film on Soho.

factsheet.heading: History
paragraphs: 75 Dean Street has long been part of Soho’s creative story. For many years it housed De Lane Lea Studios, one of London’s most influential recording and post-production facilities. Countless musicians, filmmakers and broadcasters passed through its doors, helping to cement Soho’s reputation as a global centre for film, music and media.
Today, 75 Dean Street has entered a new chapter. The building is home to the Museum of Soho and a growing cultural community through All is Joy, providing space for emerging creatives.
For Open House, we have talks on the Saints and Sinners of Soho, West End Musical Theatre,  Hedonism and Activism and the award winning short documentary, Our Soho.

Interspersed will be short films from Fealy Films.  Angela Fealy is currently pulling together the 12 x 12 project to work with up and coming working class filmmakers  with the ambitious aim of helping them to create 12 short films in 2026 with 8 in the can already!
